More formally, given two complementary product pairs \((x, z)\) and \((y, z)\), the traditional one-to-one mapping approaches necessarily yield close Euclidean distances \(d(x, z)\) and \(d(y, z)\), which further implies that the distance \(d(x, y)\) is also close under the representation space in use. However, in reality, products \(x\) and \(y\) could be substitute, complementary or even non-related. Therefore, existing one-to-one product-to-representation mapping approaches are fundamentally inadequate to precisely describe the complementary relations in e-commerce recommender systems.

item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports distinguishing directional transitions from simple item similarity. [GaGNN (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002002552400536X) combines individual and group transition graphs to address sparse sequences. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary products through both relevance and dissimilarity, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters. [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://assets.amazon.science/6f/7c/c7e95c1141f7b81eab3d0d782443/transitivity-encoded-graph-attention-networks-for-complementary-item-recommendations.pdf) uses separate key/value representations to capture non-transitive complement relationships and incorporates substitute-graph supervision. Its substitute labels are unavailable here, so that component cannot be transferred directly.\n\nText-aware sequential research often assumes external pretrained encoders: [ST2SI (COLING 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/) explicitly learns item transitions through text-to-ID mapping but relies on LLMs. These results do not establish that locally learned title/description features alone will help sparse interactions. A practical hypothesis for this benchmark: construct a directed transition graph exclusively from training histories; learn separate source/target embeddings; encode titles/descriptions with randomly initialized token embeddings and pooled text features; fuse graph, text and SASRec scores through a small learned gate. Text should share evidence across rare items rather than impose similarity as the recommendation objective. Compare against transition-only and text-only ablations using macro validation HR@10. Treat complementarity, compatibility and ownership redundancy as unobserved hypotheses—neither temporal succession nor lexical similarity establishes those relationships."}
